content:
#1 While skyrmion approaches are promising for nonperturbative models of particles, the original ones seem to hit a wall - interpreting topological charge as baryon number.

But there are rising liquid-crystal-like approaches reinterpreting topological charge as elementary electric charge instead - interpreting curvature of some deeper field as electric field, Gauss law counts topological charge of this deeper field (becomes Gauss-Bonnet), leading to EM with built-in charge quantization as topological.

In liquid crystals they experimentally get Coulomb-like interaction for them (e.g. nature.com/articles/s41598-017-16200-z, 10.1103/PhysRevE.76.011707 ), it also brings regularization of singularity in agreement with running coupling effect (e.g. mdpi.com/2218-1997/11/4/113).

Then there appear topological vortices, in particle physics corresponding to quark string/gluon flux tube (e.g. sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370269399012083 ), e.g. decaying into particles in string hadronization used to model LHC collisions, forming various size knots - resembling various size nuclei (e.g. nature.com/articles/s41567-025-03107-0 )

Also Einstein’s teleparallelism is practically 4D liquid crystal - suggesting natural unification with gravity through boosts of 0th: time axis.

Here is my approach to formalize it into model of particles, using skyrme-like kinetic Lagrangian term, with liquid-crystal-like Landau-de Gennes field and Higgs-like potential: arxiv.org/pdf/2108.07896. Conference slides and recording: indico.slu.cz/event/34/contributions/396/

Would gladly discuss/collaborate on this growing branch/reinterpretation of skyrmion approaches.
subject: Liquid-crystal-like skyrmion models of particles?

content:
#2 Polite suggestion: Omit the sentence about teleparallel gravity: It makes no sense as stated, neither in itself nor in this context.

For the rest of #1, the combination of keywords is vaguely plausible and potentially interesting, though this impression gets challenged when opening your slides.
subject: Liquid-crystal-like skyrmion models of particles?

content:
#3 Einstein’s teleparallelism, as attempt to unify EM+gravity, is field of 4 orthogonal vector fields forming tetrad - like 4D liquid crystal. The mistake he made was assuming equal length for 4 vectors - it is crucial to distinguish them, e.g. like in Landau-de Gennes basic model for liquid crystals. For example hedgehog of spatial vector is topological charge getting Coulomb interaction like electron, while hedgehog of temporal vector would be a black hole - needs much larger Lagrangian contributions.

Liquid crystal groups recently pursue such particle physics interpretations: from quantized topological charges with Coulomb-like interaction, to vortices/knots interpreted as e.g. nuclei. Since 2009 I slowly try to formalize it: getting topological excitations-particle physics correspondence with at least qualitatively looking perfect agreement, and recently quantitatively combining Skyrme kinetic term with Landau-de Gennes field and potential.

This directions finally allows to get nonperturbative field configurations of particles - e.g. electron with quantized charge, magnetic dipole and angular momentum, proton lighter than neutron, deuteron with quadrupole moment, etc. But quantitatively it needs really tough simulations - tensor field with nonlinear potential, resting e.g. electron is already dynamical due to angular momentum …
subject: Liquid-crystal-like skyrmion models of particles?

content: #4 No, the tetrad formulation of GR is general (cf. first-order formulation of gravity) and not specific to teleparallel gravity. And it makes no sense to postfix either form of gravity with the words “like 4D liquid crystal”.
subject: Liquid-crystal-like skyrmion models of particles?

content:
#5 In basic liquid crystal model there is field of 3 orthogonal axes packed into 3x3 matrix: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landau%E2%80%93de_Gennes_theory.

In 4D spacetime we need to extend it to real symmetric 4x4 tensor field - which (usually different) 4 eigenvectors form tetrad.

Landau-de Gennes uses Higgs-like potential preferring some its eigenspectrum - like preferred shape of molecule, which can be deformed especially in the center of topological excitations to regularize e.g. charge to finite energy (deforming Coulomb interaction in agreement with the running coupling effect).

Using skyrmion kinetic term in such 4D Landau-de Gennes model, its (Goldstone) SO(1,3) vacuum dynamics (in minimum of potential) unify EM+QM+GEM:

  • rotations of the longest spatial axis get Maxwell equations for EM, with quantized electric charge as topological,

  • twists of this longest axis get much lower Lagrangian contributions, get Klein-Gordon-like equation as quantum phase, rotating e.g. for angular momentum of electron,

  • boosts of much longer temporal axis get second set of Maxwell equations - of GEM: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravitoelectromagnetism.

There also appear various interactions between them, like slowing down of EM propagation in gravitational field like in (originally Einstein’s) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variable_speed_of_light - leading to gravitational time dilation, and light bending by Fermat principle.

Another type of their interaction brings energetic tendency for local boosts in presence of spatial derivatives (particle gravitational mass), and for time derivatives for e.g. angular momentum of electron and neutrino oscillations - making them oscillating already in the lowest energy state, as in the original definition of time crystals.
subject: Liquid-crystal-like skyrmion models of particles?

content:
#6 Also a polite suggestion from me: When I saw the first text, before seeing you had papers on arXiv, I had dismissed it as pure AI slop. Already the first two sentences include “- interpreting” to add a comment, later also “- suggesting”, your second message yet again opens like that in the first two sentences while both the second and third close like that (I’ve not read anything inbetween in detail) — suggesting the well-known typical style of AI. And there are other hints like the bullet point list in your third message or the fact that both the second and third message are not even proper responses to the messages before.

Stuff like this makes people not want to spend their time with the content, even if there was something useful buried in there. Especially in mathematics and physics, AI is known to hallucinate, but then to deliver its wrong claims with absolute confidence. Chat GPT for example has already told me that x2=xx^2=xx2=x in general, came up with a phantom chapter title of a textbook available online and even quoted theorems with explicit numbers from it, which in reality stated something totally different. Please be aware of that! Chatbots produce text that LOOKS like plausible and real science, not IS it.

#7 Hello, I slowly work on such models of particles since 2009 (v1 of arXiv:0910.2724), as one of many topics simultaneously (my webpage), and never used LLMs for articles, I have PhD in computer science (2010) and in physics (2012), also MSc in math.

While there are now lots of liquid crystal articles showing similarity with particle physics, my main article on this topic is arXiv/2108.07896 - seems you refer to “interpreting field curvature as electric field”, which is absolutely crucial here for charge quantization, making Gauss law count topological charge (becomes en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauss%E2%80%93Bonnet_theorem. Regarding “suggesting”, I see it refers to experimental recreation of similar behavior in liquid crystal - it is tough to use a stronger word, generally this is search in progress - requires careful wording.

Here is a lighter introduction with code: https://community.wolfram.com/groups/-/m/t/2856493 , talk: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MgSLyfb92B4.

#9 Thank you, I would gladly discuss, maybe collaborate. My approach for such liquid-crystal-like models of particles is 4D Landau-de Gennes field and potential, with skyrmion kinetic term. I collaborate e.g. with Manfried Faber, who has slightly simplified model, getting e.g. running coupling Coulomb corrections from regularizing charges: mdpi.com/2218-1997/11/4/113. I have contact with skyrmion society, but they are completely fixed on their interpretation (topological charge as baryon number, while we as quantized electric charge).

I have started such considerations from studying Maximal Entropy Random Walk (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximal_entropy_random_walk), which shows that properly made diffusion - according to maximal entropy principle crucial for statistical physics, it no longer disagrees with quantum predictions, also getting Born rule/Bell violation.
